summary: A searchable, multi-select filter. The trigger keeps its label and shows how many are chosen; nothing applies until Apply.

pairs.dont: Replace the trigger's label with the chosen values.
pairs.do: Keep the label ('Filter actions…') and let the count badge say how many.
pairs.why: Three values will not fit a 240px trigger, and a truncated list reads as one value. The label says what the filter is; the count says it is on.

pairs.dont: Apply each tick as it happens.
pairs.do: Collect ticks in a draft and commit once on Apply.
pairs.why: Every tick in a filter re-queries the table behind it. Four live ticks are four reloads and a table jumping under the cursor.

pairs.dont: Keep a half-finished draft after Escape or a click away.
pairs.do: Treat closing without Apply as Cancel.
pairs.why: Someone who closes the menu without applying has changed their mind. Keeping the draft surprises them the next time they open it.

pairs.dont: Show 30 options as one flat list.
pairs.do: Give options a group, and let search do the rest.
pairs.why: Group labels turn scanning into skipping. Past about eight options, people search rather than scroll — the search box is focused on open for that reason.

pairs.dont: Use Select for a choice of two or three.
pairs.do: Use a RadioGroup or a ButtonGroup.
pairs.why: A menu hides the options behind a click. With three, showing them all is faster and needs no search.

a11y: The search is a combobox that owns the list through aria-activedescendant, so focus never leaves it: ArrowUp/Down move, Enter ticks, Ctrl/⌘+Enter applies, Escape closes.
Options are role=option with aria-selected in an aria-multiselectable listbox. The checkbox is drawn, not a real control, so each row is announced once.
The count badge is aria-hidden; the trigger's name includes ', N selected' as text.
